blockers.summary: 7 assembly bodies have no recorded weight, so the total mass and centre of gravity are incomplete: Avionics_Bay:1, Body39, Body49, CLAMP_FOILROOT_R_V3:1, CLAMP_X_B38-B39_R:1, CLAMP_X_B45-B39_L:1, FRONT_JET_TILT30:1.
blockers.required_evidence: Measured mass of each listed body, or explicit confirmation that it is not fitted in the flight configuration being simulated.

blockers.summary: The only EDF thrust data is a manufacturer maximum-thrust figure; there is no measured command-to-thrust curve.
blockers.required_evidence: Thrust-stand sweep of commanded input against steady thrust across the supported voltage and inflow envelope, with test conditions and instrument tolerances.

blockers.summary: No measured reaction-torque coefficient; the source data sets km to zero. All ten fans turn the same way, so the reaction torques add rather than cancel, and at hover they are a constant yaw bias the two tilted front fans must hold against for the whole flight. Modelling km as zero hides that bias completely in simulation: the first place it appears is on the aircraft.
blockers.required_evidence: Thrust-stand torque measurement giving km for one fan of each installed type. The rotation sense is now recorded. Analysis at the hover trim gives the front pair +/-5.70 N.m of yaw authority; km up to 0.030 m keeps the standing bias inside 58% of it, so the measurement decides how much margin is left rather than whether the aircraft can hold heading at all.

blockers.summary: No measured EDF spin-up or spin-down response.
blockers.required_evidence: Step-response measurement of commanded input against thrust for the XFly Galaxy X8 80mm on the Flycolor X-Cross HV3 160A ESC, at the ramp and timing the ESC is actually programmed with, giving a time constant with its confidence interval.

blockers.summary: Foil hinge origins, axes and mechanical travel limits are not in the CAD export; it provides jet-channel centroids only.
blockers.required_evidence: Hinge origin and axis in the body FRD frame, the zero reference, the positive sense and the mechanical travel limits from the installation drawing.

blockers.summary: The aircraft turns each duct jet with a foil, so the effective thrust vector depends on foil deflection through a Coanda-type interaction. No validated model or dataset relates deflection to turned-jet force and loss.
blockers.required_evidence: Bench or wind-tunnel measurement of resultant force magnitude and direction against foil deflection across the supported range, or a CFD campaign validated against such measurements.

blockers.summary: No body or surface aerodynamic coefficient dataset exists.
blockers.required_evidence: Coefficient tables with reference geometry, conventions, Reynolds and Mach range, interpolation rule and declared valid envelope.

blockers.summary: No measured avionics mounting poses for the IMU, magnetometer, barometer or GNSS antenna.
blockers.required_evidence: Sensor translations and orientations in the body FRD frame from the avionics installation drawing.

blockers.summary: Front-motor sideways-tilt axis and mechanical travel limits are not recorded in the CAD export.
blockers.required_evidence: Tilt pivot axis in the body FRD frame, its zero reference and the mechanical travel limits.

blockers.summary: Sensor noise density is now measured, but in-run bias stability is not: the static recording's low-frequency band was dominated by movement of the surface the board sat on, which is the same band bias instability occupies.
blockers.required_evidence: A static high-rate recording on a decoupled surface, ideally a concrete floor with nobody in the room, long enough for an Allan deviation minimum to appear. FIFO logging for the ADIS16470 and ICM-45686 as well, since only the IIM-42652 is currently characterised.

blockers.summary: The simulated IMU carries white Gaussian noise at the measured static noise density. A running EDF produces narrow-band vibration at blade-pass frequency and its harmonics, which is a different thing entirely: it aliases into the gyro and accelerometer, drives the rate controller's derivative term, and can make the estimator diverge. Nothing in the simulator can produce this, so a controller that is stable in simulation says nothing about whether it is stable on a running aircraft.
blockers.required_evidence: High-rate IMU logging with the fans running at several throttle settings, on the aircraft, with its actual mounting. Enough to show where the blade-pass peaks land relative to the gyro filter cutoffs and whether the estimator holds.

blockers.summary: No ground-effect model exists. Close to a surface the ten jets recirculate and the thrust each fan produces at a given command changes, asymmetrically and with height. Every planned first test happens within a metre of the floor, which is exactly where the effect is largest and where the simulator is silent.
blockers.required_evidence: Thrust or attitude response measured at several heights above a surface, or a validated ground-effect model for a ducted-fan array over a foil.

blockers.summary: Each of the eight foil fans is modelled as acting alone, and the total force is their sum. They blow on one shared foil, so their jets meet on it. The simulator therefore cannot show a jet being deflected by its neighbour, nor a Coanda attachment failing on one station because of what the next one is doing.
blockers.required_evidence: Measured force and moment for combinations of fans running together, not only one at a time, over the throttle range the aircraft actually uses.

blockers.summary: Thrust in the model depends only on the command. On the aircraft it also depends on pack voltage, which falls through a flight and falls further under load, so the command that hovers at the start does not hover at the end. The simulator holds a constant relationship and so cannot show the drift.
blockers.required_evidence: Thrust measured against command at several pack voltages across the usable range, or a voltage-compensated thrust model with its coefficients measured.

blockers.summary: The command the model uses is a normalised number from zero to one that maps straight to thrust. On the aircraft it passes through a Flycolor X-Cross HV3 ESC with its own idle point, its own throttle curve and its own ramp limiting, none of which is recorded. A mismatch at the low end matters most, because that is where the rotation on the rig is commanded from.
blockers.required_evidence: The ESC's configured protocol, idle throttle, startup power and any ramp limiting, plus a command-to-RPM measurement through the installed ESC.

blockers.summary: The simulated magnetometer reads a clean uniform field. On the aircraft it sits near wiring carrying hundreds of amps, whose field varies with throttle, so heading error becomes a function of how hard the aircraft is working. With no GNSS the magnetometer is the only heading reference there is.
blockers.required_evidence: Magnetometer readings logged against throttle with the aircraft restrained, showing how much the indicated heading moves between idle and hover power.

blockers.summary: The simulated pivot passes exactly through the centre of gravity and has no friction and no inertia, which is why gravity produced no moment about it and the aircraft's rotation was its own. A physical base whose pivot is not at the centre of gravity adds a gravity moment that grows with angle, and its friction and inertia change the rotation the controller sees. None of that is recorded.
blockers.required_evidence: The pivot axis position relative to the aircraft's centre of gravity, the friction at the pivot and the rig's own rotational inertia.

blockers.summary: The aircraft is simulated as one rigid body. It is a carbon structure carrying ten fans on booms and a foil spanning them, so under thrust the fans do not stay where the geometry says they are, and the structure has bending modes the IMU will see. The simulator has no deformation and no modes, so it cannot show a control loop interacting with one.
blockers.required_evidence: Measured deflection of the booms and foil under representative thrust, and the first structural mode frequencies, to compare against the control bandwidth.
